title: Model feature descriptor API and version affinity for onboarding
creator: Priya Nair
description: Define and implement a new, backward-compatible API surface for publishing machine-readable model feature descriptors and per-model version affinity hints. The descriptor exposes limits (max_tokens, rate_limits), capabilities (chat, streaming, function_calling), context_window profiles, and performance profiles (latency/throughput buckets). Version affinity allows serving/runtime to express preferred or guaranteed binary versions for routing and pinning logic.
acceptance_criteria: Schema v1 for feature_descriptor is published to the /models/{model_id}/descriptor endpoint and documented in the developer API spec
Runtime consumes version_affinity hints to prefer pinned binaries when available; fallbacks respected according to policy
Model onboarding flow (web UI + CLI) can upload descriptor JSON and surface validation errors
Backward-compatibility: adding optional fields does not break clients; deprecated fields are rejected with warnings
Automated integration tests validate that performance_profile buckets map to runtime kernel-selection heuristics
Docs and examples (OpenAPI fragments + sample JSON) available in Confluence and included in SDK generation pipeline
implementation_notes: We will introduce a lightweight JSON contract: feature_descriptor { id, public_name, version_tag, capabilities:[], limits:{max_tokens,context_window,concurrent_requests}, performance_profiles:[{name,sequence_length_dist,median_latency_ms,throughput_rps}], version_affinity:{preferred:[version_ids],strict:false,affinity_score:0-100} }. Keep fields optional when possible. Use semantic version tags for affinity and include a checksum field for binary mapping. Runtime will add a read-only ingestion_report embedding observed metrics. Validation occurs in onboarding lambda; schema validated via JSON Schema v7 and included in SDK types. Avoid tightly coupling to manifest V2; descriptor is additive.
api_contract_examples: PUT /api/v1/models/{model_id}/descriptor (multipart upload + JSON) - returns 202 with validation_report_id
migration_plan: Phase 1: Publish schema as descriptor_v1 and allow ingest path; runtime ignores unknown optional fields (backwards-compatible)
Phase 2: Update onboarding UI/CLI to submit descriptors and surface validation warnings
Phase 3: Runtime implements affinity handling in routing layer behind a feature flag; we monitor routing success and regression metrics for 2 weeks
Phase 4: Enable affinity by default for eligible customers and update SDKs + documentation
Rollback: If regression > 5% P99 latency increase or error-rate spike, flip affinity feature flag off and revert ingestion acceptance for strict affinity
risks: Exposing a rich descriptor could create tight coupling between external orchestration and our internal kernel selection if fields are misinterpreted
Incorrect affinity settings could increase error rates if preferred binaries are unhealthy
Backward compatibility mistakes may break third-party clients depending on legacy manifest fields
Security: descriptors may reveal capacity/limits that adversaries could use for targeted abuse
links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2543 (draft PR for descriptor schema and ingestion lambda)
